query: How do review themes differ between positive and negative Yelp sentiment?

per_column.name: staff_attentiveness
per_column.rationale: A service theme external to sentiment with interpretable categories (friendly, helpful, attentive vs not_present). Can be segmented and compared against label_pos to reveal how service themes differ by sentiment.

per_column.name: food_taste_quality
per_column.rationale: Well-separated valenced categories (delicious, excellent vs mediocre, bland) forming a clear taste theme that plausibly correlates with and can be grouped against sentiment.

per_column.name: food_freshness
per_column.rationale: Interpretable freshness theme (fresh vs old, cold, overcooked). Distinct from taste; supports meaningful segmentation against label_pos.

per_column.name: portion_size
per_column.rationale: Interpretable quantity theme (generous, adequate vs small, microscopic) that can be compared across sentiment groups.

per_column.name: food_freshness_issue
per_column.rationale: Near-duplicate of food_freshness with essentially identical value distribution; adds no new relationship, merely restates an existing added column.

per_column.name: portion_size_satisfaction
per_column.rationale: Redundant with portion_size, sharing the same category vocabulary and distribution; contributes no additional interpretable dimension.

judge.rationale: The set successfully decomposes review content into distinct, interpretable theme dimensions (service attentiveness, taste, freshness, portion size), each with well-separated valenced categories that can be grouped and compared against the label_pos focus to explore how themes differ by sentiment. This directly serves the exploratory query. However, two of the six columns are near-exact duplicates of others (food_freshness_issue ≈ food_freshness; portion_size_satisfaction ≈ portion_size), inflating the column count without opening new relationships. The heavy 'not_present' skew in some columns (staff_attentiveness, portion_size) limits comparative power for the minority categories. Net: a genuinely informative EDA schema partially weakened by redundancy.
